newsitem.title: FINLAND: MARKKA BONDS END SOLID AFTER RECORD 2006 AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: MARKKA BONDS END SOLID AFTER RECORD 2006 AUCTION.

text.p: Bonds ended solid, defying
weakness overseas, after a record heavily bid auction of the
benchmark 2006 bolstered sentiment, dealers said.
"This (auction) took the market by surprise," one dealer
said, adding that there were no fundamental reasons for the
bullish tone and "no reason to get positive about Finland."
The auction drew bids of 7.6 billion markka, of which 3.3
billion markka worth were accepted at a yield of 6.29 percent.
But dealers and analysts said that the long-end spread to
Germany, after some slight narrowing today, could easily head
the other way tomorrow if overseas sentiment remained bearish.
Participants in the auction included few end-investors, while many of the bids stemmed from shortcovering or came from primary dealers or London houses, one market analyst said.
"There has been a shortage of bonds in recent weeks. That has squeezed the market, and narrowed the spread (over Germany)," he said.
Dealers said that while the 2006 auction stole the show, there was also some other buying interest in the long end.
The markka was unmoved by volatility in the Swedish crown caused by jitters over Sweden's position on EMU, dealers said.
"The markka doesn't react to anything," one analyst said.
DEM/FIM stuck to its recent 3.015-3.020 trading range, and
was seen staying their tomorrow, though perhaps pushing the
upper edge of that range, forex dealers said.
